parsed.explanation: The dossier shows no trans-specific criminal law, no documented police, border, or arrest targeting, and no legal barrier to facilities, care, or employment, so severity after outing is mostly social rather than state. Official Pride endorsement and health/protection decrees explicitly naming transgender people are positive climate signals. But protections for gender identity are incomplete and unenforced in the record: general anti-discrimination and hate-crime laws omit GI, sectoral rules mostly cover SO, public services/medical centres reportedly involve verbal abuse and discrimination, and violence against trans people is documented as family/community. No trans visitor incidents are documented, so these are local/hostility risks reaching care/services rather than state targeting. Border, custody, and emergency-care practices are unknown open questions, not exposures. Net: no universal restriction but weak recourse and uneven acceptance, at the elevated/reduced boundary.
